After a two-year gap, Apple is developing a new-generation iMac powered by the M6 chip and featuring fresh colour options, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman. The new machine is expected to launch "before the end of the year."

The iMac's update cycle has never been particularly frequent — it skipped both the M2 and M5 chip generations, and a larger screen size has yet to materialise, with Apple steering pro users towards the Mac Studio or a Mac mini paired with a Studio Display. Still, Apple is preparing a new iMac with the M6 chip.

Gurman says this update will bring "several brand-new colours," though he offered no details. The 2024 M4 model only made minor tweaks to the colour lineup, keeping the same seven colour choices but adjusting the shades. The new iMac is also expected to go on sale before the end of the year:

Meaning this autumn could be a significant one for the Mac, with — alongside the potential M6-equipped iMac — an anticipated lineup that may include: a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen and tandem OLED; a new 14-inch MacBook Pro running the M6; and a new Mac Studio featuring the M5 Max and M5 Ultra (supply permitting). A new M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini is also a possibility, though it's expected to arrive a little later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip produced on the new 2nm process, but there will reportedly be no M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra variants — Apple plans to accelerate the rollout of the M7 series.
